newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Aug wage settlements average 1.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Aug wage settlements average 1.2 pct.

text.p: Annual wage increases in Canadian collective bargaining agreements reached in August rose to an 1.2 percent from 0.7 percent in July, the Department of Human Resources Development said on Thursday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast only a 0.8 percent increase in wage settlements in August.
It marked the highest increase in private sector wage settlements since the 2.4 percent registered in October 1995.

The overall increase of 1.2 percent was the highest since the 1.3 percent registered in April 1996, a department official said. He cautioned however that the results were based on a below-average number of agreements and employees.

Wage increases are the average annual percentage increase in base rates -- the wage rate of the lowest paid classification in a bargaining unit -- over the term of the agreement in settlements negotiated during the period shown.
The private sector rise was well above the July average for the sector of 0.8 percent and the year-to-date average of 1.2 percent and the 1.4 percent average for 1995 as a whole.
Settlements in the manufacturing sector, mainly in pulp and paper, with an average of 2.6 percent, accounted for much of the private sector gain in August.

In the public sector, adjustments ranged from wage freezes in eight of the 13 settlements, including 1,400 teachers in an Ontario school board and 700 academic staff at Carleton University, to a 2.5 percent increase for 600 operations employees with Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro.
